restrictions: Generic, distribution-free birthday attack; uses no structural property of 32-round SHA-256 and produces no concrete collision.
Complete analytic candidate; charged time is a worst-case upper bound over the algorithm's own coins, not a full-scale execution.

The declared accounting is REGISTER-FREE: every two-input gate is charged load + load + operation + store, so the entire 256-to-768-word bitsliced working state is materialized in RAM and no bounded register file is assumed. There is no register-residency premise. A tighter register-resident figure (125.983) is reported as an explicitly optional variant the claim does not rely on.

Each of the q records stores three 256-bit words (digest, u, v); the per-record cost charges the packed compression, the digest transpose, the message-identity transpose that materializes (u, v), the record store, the register-free loop-control overhead of every non-unrolled pass, and the counting-sort grouping over the three-word records; the proof enumerates every cost-model primitive category and shows each is charged.

The compression gate count is charged on the fully hand-derivable UNFOLDED basis (56,224 compression gates + 8,192 digest-transpose + 16,384 message-transpose per batch), matched to the last gate by an inlined instrumented counter; every loop has a compile-time-fixed trip count with no data-dependent branch, so the total is exactly (per-record count) times q, an identity rather than an extrapolation.

Declared time_log2 = 127.7 is a conservative upper bound over every register-free row, including the per-bit-plane rotation surcharge (127.665); it remains below the prior generic exponent 128.22 by about 0.52 bit.
